utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we continue, Ms. Pilipovic, your next witness, as we understand, is a witness for whom protective measures have been requested, although on the last list attached to the letter of the 22nd of November, it does not appear that protective measures have been sought. But if I'm -- at the same time, I see that this witness appears as number 4 in the observations of the Defence in respect of the decision of the Chamber of the 19th November. Is that correct? Do we find --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It's a submission in French dated the 12th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Of the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. A small puzzle every morning keeps us awake.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think I said the 20th of November. I see that by mistake says the 12th. I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, since the Prosecution has had no opportunity yet to express tself on the additional reasons given in the submission of the 20th of November, is there any observations you'd like to make in respect of the protective measures sought?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the protective measures will be granted. And perhaps I repeat that one of the reasons why the Chamber grants these measures also because they are limited in their effect. That means that the testimony as such as a whole is audible; it's just facial distortion and pseudonym. When I say "just," it's not to indicate that it is not an important measure, but there are other measures that are affecting the publicity of the trial to a far greater extent. Ms. Pilipovic, is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might I raise a few matters very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We have received over the past week or so a number of expert reports from the Defence. Some of that material is in the Russian language and in B/C/S which presents a difficulty to us. The Prosecution takes the view that the material should be filed in a language of the Tribunal and therefore requests that the Defence be required to provide that part or those parts of the reports which are in Russian or B/C/S in either English or French, preferably English. That's the first issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you a question first. Are you talking about the reports itself or about the supporting material?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Annexes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The second issue concerns the order of the Court that the Defence provide to the Prosecution the dates of birth and addresses and paternal family names of the witnesses to be called. We raised with the Defence last week that we are running out of such information, and they directed us to a letter they had sent some weeks ago. We'll check that, and the situation at the moment is that we only have dates of birth for the witnesses to be called this week, and I think one next week. Mr. President, that does impact significantly on our ability to carry out our inquiries before witnesses are called. I therefore respectfully request that the Defence be obliged to comply with that earlier order in relation to all of the remaining witnesses within a matter of days. Mr. President, the third issue concerns the sittings in January. I would be grateful if the Defence could provide us with the pertinent information for the witnesses to be called in the first week well before the standard seven days which, of course, would fall over the holiday period. It would be helpful to us if we could have that material in December, preferably early December, so that we can complete our inquiries in time for that week and make arrangements for that first sitting week. Mr. President, the next issue concerns the witness that was called last Friday, that's DP53. Mr. President, you may recall that at the end, towards the end of his evidence, he revealed that the date on which he was wounded was the date of one of the scheduled sniping incidents. That had not been brought out in chief, only that he had been wounded with no reference to the date. As it transpires, that's a matter of some significance. The witness has gone. It would be helpful to the Prosecution to have sufficient information in relation to the treatment that the witness received for his wound so that the Prosecution can make its own inquiries with a view to confirming the date on which he was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Redaction be made. And could we turn into closed session -- private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session again. Then the next issue was whether the Defence could provide the Prosecution with any details in respect of the medical treatment of Witness DP53. I take it that this might need some further inquiries so that you'll first inform the Prosecution what would be possible or not. And if this would not give a positive result, then the Chamber will certainly hear of it, I take it. Then the third issue -- the third issue was sittings in January, witnesses to be called, whether you could provide the Prosecution timely with a list. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I then take it that you say that you could meet this request of the Prosecution. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour. I think that it could be the 11th or 12th of December, as I have been informed we won't be working on those days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, 11th, I think I indicated that the parties should keep themselves ready. I'm not saying that we are sitting, but should keep themselves ready to sit. You'll hear about that soon. There's another issue. When we are talking about sitting in the month of January, the Chamber has considered that it might be very, very inconvenient, especially for witnesses, to come on the 6th and the 7th of January. The 7th -- 6th of January being the first day after the recess, and the 7th of January being Orthodox Christmas. So therefore, the Chamber is very much inclined and has given it some consideration not to sit on the 6th and the 7th of January for these reasons. And this would be finalised in one or two days, so you'll hear about it soon. But we --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. But I'd be grateful if you could consider the question of whether we'll be working on the 8th or whether it's on the 7th. That's when the witnesses should be coming. The Orthodox Christmas is on the 7th. Could you consider this question. Then the first working day would be the 9th, and that means they would be able to travel on the 8th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's three days, and as you -- the mere fact that we come up with the issue on the 6th and the -- about the 6th and the 7th by ourselves, that means that the Chamber is taking this quite seriously and wants to take into consideration the problems that might arise from sitting on the 6th and the 7th. Would it not be possible to call perhaps witnesses that would not come from the Former Yugoslavia on the 8th so that we could continue. Because I do understand the problems you might have, but there might be -- I saw that on your list, although at that time it was not quite clear to us whether you approached these witnesses already, but there were witnesses also that do not come from the Former Yugoslavia and might not be bound by the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So three days would be perhaps a bit too much. Then --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Defence counsel will be informed after the 15th of December about the possibility of other witnesses coming who won't be coming from the territory of the Former Yugoslavia. So we can solve this problem in the way that you have suggested. So the 8th would then be a working day. The 8th of January would then be the first working day if I have understood this correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what we had in mind until now, but I will inform you finally on the 6th and 7th of January soon. Then the dates of birth of witnesses, I take it Ms. Pilipovic that the Prosecution will be informed about the dates of birth on very short notice. They are running out of --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm looking at the submission of the 12th November, 2002, which I provided to my learned colleagues. And I would like to have a short meeting so that we can see which witnesses are concerned, the witnesses whose dates of birth and place of residence have not been provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I take it this could be solved on very short--

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we did a close analysis of that list, although at first glance it contains a lot of information, some 21 witnesses and so on, in fact all it has in addition to what we previously had are three dates of birth and that's it. No fresh addresses, no fresh -- oh, and some new addresses. So Mr. President, we do at this stage seek a direction that the Defence provide that material by a particular date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would first like to see whether both parties could agree on what's missing and whether there is a problem. If there's a problem, I take it that if dates of birth and addresses have been provided, of course there's no problem. You can check that, I would say, together. And if they are not provided, they should be provided so that the --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This is what I'm suggesting. Your Honours, I accept your proposal, bearing in mind the fact that the last submission dated the 12th of November contains a lot of information. But I'm willing to discuss the matter with my colleagues and to try to solve this problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you can reach no agreement in order to make it possible for the Chamber to give further guidance to the parties, I would then like to receive a copy indicating what is missing so that we know what is just a small number of data or whether it's really substantial. Then the final issue, the material in English, the annexes to the expert reports. Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Defence counsel has provided the expert report in the official language of the Tribunal, in English. And I accept that certain documents which were attached to the expert report, original documents, and there are certain documents which are in the Russian language. If my learned colleagues insist on having certain texts and articles translated into one of the official languages of the Tribunal, I can solve this problem, too. My colleague and I will sit down, and we will solve this problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is my recollection right, Mr. Ierace, that some of the annexes to the Prosecution expert reports were not in English and/or French, but were not attached to the reports?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, some of the annexes were in B/C/S which is, of course, the language of the accused and a language spoken and read by counsel for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The only other material in a different language was the original of the report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Hungarian report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, whilst I'm on my feet, can I just pick up on one other issue. Madam Pilipovic proposes that we be informed of the identity of the witnesses for the first week after we finish sitting Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in December. I'd be grateful if the date by which we are to be informed could be at least 24 hours before we finish sitting in case there are any issues to be raised. I would be grateful if the witnesses to be called in those few days were not major witnesses. I note that DP51 is to be recalled. He said that he would be available in that week, that's for his cross-examination to be completed. I will not be here that week, and whilst I have a very capable team, I'd be grateful if we did not have a major witness in that week, in those few days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, the Chamber is not very much aware of what are major witnesses and what are not, but perhaps if you sit together and if Ms. Pilipovic would make a proposal on what witnesses to call that week, you'll have a better idea on whether you will consider them major witnesses or not and see whether you can agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If not, then of course we could see whether the Chamber could assist you in reaching an agreement. But I then, Ms. Pilipovic, hear that you are willing to cooperate, provide the material, as good as possible in one of the official languages of the Tribunal. If there are any other questions in relation to these witness reports -- of the expert reports, the Chamber, of course, started looking at them as well. Perhaps you should deal with that before the recess starts. Is there any other issue? Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Your Honours, I just want to inform my learned colleague that the Witness DP51 whose cross-examination has to be finished by my colleague will be scheduled for next week. Last night I sent the schedule for next week since we are working on Tuesday and Wednesday and Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that's new information for you, Mr. Ierace. If there's nothing else, I would first like to ask whether the protective measures are in effect, that means face distortion. What would be the pseudonym, Ms. Pilipovic? I just look at my list, and would think it would be DP50. Is that correct? DP50.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you -- from your answer, I take it that you can hear me in a language you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving testimony in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration. Mr. DP50, because that's how we will call you because of the protective measures that have been granted in respect of you, Mr. DP50, may I invite you to make that solemn declaration of which the text will now be handed to you by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. DP50. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will first be examined by counsel for the Defence. Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. DP50, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Before I start asking you questions, I'm going to show you a document. And I'd like you to tell us and confirm whether the information contained on the sheet of paper that you'll be handed is correct. Mr. DP50, did you have a look at the information on that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is the information correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps it would be a good time to go into private session so that Mr. DP50 can give us more detailed information regarding himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, please, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, you told us where you were born, where you lived, and where you worked. I'd just like to tell you before we start asking the questions, we will be speaking about the period from September 1992 until August 1994. And during this period of time, were you present at this area where you said that you lived and you worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, did you serve in the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What is your military specialty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I'm an artillery man.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In September 1992, were you militarily engaged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I was in the Zuc hill area as an ordinary private. I was in a trench.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When I told you in the beginning, we will be speaking about the period from September 1992 to August 1994, can you tell us whether throughout this period you were engaged in this area? Or did your deployment change in a sense that you were a soldier in the trench?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I was in the trench until September 1992. In September, I was injured, and I was on sick leave, so to speak, until January 1993. And then since my military specialty was that of an artillery man, I was called by the ministry of defence, I was told to go and get my new schedule, my new deployment schedule. And I was transferred to an artillery unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, in January 1993, when you say that you were transferred to an artillery unit, did you stay in this unit until August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Since your military specialty was artillery, in January 1993, what was the weapon that you were issued with in your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I was issued with a cannon, 76-millimetre, M42 Zis.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, I'll just quickly go back to September 1992 for continuity's purposes. You belonged to a certain military unit in 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what was the military unit, the formation in that area at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: At that time, there was a Krivoglavci Battalion. I was in the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: This Krivoglavci Battalion, within which military formation was it part of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: It was part of the Vogosca Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us you were the 2nd Company.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: This 2nd Company, do you know when was it established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When did you first join this company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: That was some time in June or July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many members did this company have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: As far as I knew, 40 to 50 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether these men were professional soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who were these men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Most of the time, these were locals, inhabitants of the settlement of Josanica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Let us be precise, when you say settlement of Josanica, is that the area of --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: That is the centre, the close centre of Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP50, when you told us that your military specialty was artillery and that you were issued with a cannon, M4 -- 76 Zis, this artillery unit that you belonged to, did it have a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: It was called a mixed artillery battery.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: This mixed artillery battery existed as part of which larger formation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Of the Mixed Artillery Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And this Mixed Artillery Battalion --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: It was part of the Vogosca Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you tell us that you were issued with this weapon, can you tell us, what is the purpose of this cannon 76 millimetre? What can you tell us, what did you do with this cannon? How did you work on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I was everything. I was loading it, and I was targeting it. I was a gunner.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: According to the rules, how many should you have to serve the cannon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Six to eight people.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what was the reason why were you both the loader and the targeter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: There were no people who were specialised in this, not enough people.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us, was this situation the same throughout the conflict, throughout the duration of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Let us be precise: When I asked you this question, I meant whether we're speaking about staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As part of your artillery unit for which you said was a battery, whether throughout the duration of the conflict this one cannon existed or did the situation change?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I was in charge of this cannon until mid-1993. There were about two or three soldiers in the meantime in the barracks in Semizovac. And there were four cannons, B1, M48. And they were not working. They were broken, and they were taken to the Hadzici technical maintenance institute where they were fixed and they were brought to my position. And that is how in the second half of 1993, I became the commanding officer of these cannons. So that means that there were four, five, or six cannons. That depended because these cannons were old and practically every ten days or so, one or two cannons had to go and they had to be taken to be fixed because they suffered from various technical problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP50, you told us that you were a commanding officer of this battery which had four to five cannons. That is, you said four, five, six cannons. How many men were members of your battery who were crews for these cannons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: This went from 15 to 18 people.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, considering your deployment at that time, can you tell us, what is the purpose of a cannon, specifically speaking about the cannon that you were issued with, 76 millimetre cannon? But before that I wanted to ask you whether all the cannons in your battery, were they all of this type?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No. There was one Zis cannon and four B1 cannons.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Technically speaking, is there a difference between these two types of cannons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Only in their range. The Zis cannon or field gun had 12 to 13 kilometres range, while B1 field gun had 7.5 to 8 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP50, let us go back to the question that I've asked you about the cannon that you were issued with, 76 millimetres Zis field gun. Can you tell us, what is the purpose of this cannon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Destroying and disabling live enemy forces. Also destroying and disabling fortified firing points, that is, bunkers and all those other means from which fire is opened, like tanks, and any anti-tank weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you told us that one of the objectives destroying enemy live forces, can you tell us, you as an artillery man, what did you mean by enemy live forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Any soldier who had weapons on him. Whether he had a uniform or civilian clothes because at the time, there were no uniforms, and people went to the front lines in civilian clothes. So even a civilian who had firearms on him was a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you tell us what, in your opinion, is enemy live forces, your explanation with regard to the uniform and the weapons that you just gave us, this, in your opinion, applies to the enemy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether this situation also applied for the weapons and the clothing, for instance, for the situation in your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: People wore what they were able to lay their hands on.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you were telling us about enemy personnel, enemy live forces, during the -- enemy manpower, during the period of September 1992 -- or rather, January 1993 until August 1994, when you were in charge of these field guns, were you in a position while you were in charge of these cannons to receive orders to fire on these targets, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Do you mean against --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Against enemy manpower.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Enemy manpower, as I said, a soldier or a civilian who is bearing firearms, they are the targets. While a civilian who has no weapons, then that person is not a target.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During the period while you were issued with the field gun, were you in a position to fire at enemy manpower, and what were the situations if you were in such situations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Since I was in the area of the defence of the Zuc hill, the soldiers, that is, the Army of BH, was visible. That is, we could see it with the binoculars. When artillery fire was opened, it was only opened on the order of the superior commands, and not in any other situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "on the order of the superior command," can you tell us in which situations did you receive orders of the superior command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: In those situations when there would be a more intense attack of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the BH Army, that is, when the commander of the line felt that the line in the Zuc hill area was at risk. And then through some, how shall I call it, structures, the chain of command, the order, would then come to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you told us about the purpose of the field gun that you were issued with, the other purpose, you said, was the destruction of fortified posts or points. Can you tell us, as far as you were concerned, as a person in charge of a 76-millimetre field gun, what were fortified positions? Or can you define for us what are these points, these posts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes. These were trenches, bunkers from which fire was opened that were covered with logs. And atop of these logs, there was soil. And it was with a naked eye that one could see them. And then during autumn and winter months when there were no more leaves, it was possible to see trenches and communication trenches of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that the purpose of the field gun was to destroy the locations from which fire was opened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And you also said anti-tank weapons, anti-armoured weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: While you were in charge of the field gun, did you receive orders to open fire towards locations where fire was opened towards us? Can you please clarify this a little.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: During the firing of the Muslim artillery, so during the firing of the Muslim artillery, it occurred, that is, I was ordered, since because before that, I had reference points, and the commander from the line would guide where the fire was coming from, either from a tank or a Howitzer or any other weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that the BH Army in that area where you were, was it equipped with these weapons? It had a tank, it had field guns, it had Howitzers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes. The tank was located in the area from the elevation point 850 until the Orlic elevation point, and in the area of the village of Jezera. The field gun, I don't know which type it was, was also located in the area of the Orlic hill or the Orlic elevation point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The last question was in leading form. The BH army, it had a tank, had field guns, it had Howitzers. I can't find by search a reference to Howitzers in the evidence of the witness before it was mentioned by Madam Pilipovic. I don't know whether the witness earlier referred to a tank and Howitzers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wouldn't the Howitzer be in the previous answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President. I see it there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, I think that in your answer, I didn't hear until the end whether you spoke about Howitzers or Howitzer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I said that I knew about a tank. Now, whether it was a field gun or whether it was a Howitzer, I don't know. Because the fire was opened on our positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP50, during the period that you were present in that area, did you open fire from your gun in the direction of other fortified points, or fortified firing positions? Were there any other sites towards which fire was opened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: There was the transport faculty or the boarding school from which fire was opened at the Vogosca/Pale Road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, so that DP50's testimony is clear to everyone, Defence has prepared a map and suggests that the working map designated as Map C should be shown to the witness so that he can point out the area that he is mentioning, that he has mentioned, the area in which he was present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Map C, Madam Registrar. That would be -- that's the large one, the 3 by 3 metres, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I apologise, C2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, could you indicate what area? Do you want the Vogosca area to be displayed, or could you please assist the usher so --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we manage to get it on the ELMO, that would be fine so that everyone can follow the testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, can you recognise the map that you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you use the pointer, which is next to you, to point to the position that you were at. Can it be seen in this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes. In the area of the Pticja Glava elevation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see this on the map, and is this elevation marked? Does it have a number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes. Elevation Pticja Glava, 805.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: For the transcript, the witness indicated elevation Pticja Glava, which is above the word Brag, above the letter R as far as I can see, to the north. Could you tell us what the altitude is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: 805. There is a green line that goes along -- goes by the number 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP50 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, since the map is 3 by 3 metres, and where this word Brag appears several times, it's just west from Vogosca where we find these words. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that would be the word Brag which is under the word Krivoglavci. Mr. DP50, you mentioned the positions of your gun, the gun that you were responsible for. Is it possible to see the fortified positions in this map, your fortified positions, the ones that you mentioned a minute ago in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you, first of all, point out the road, could you point to the road and the transport faculty. You said that these positions were firing positions for you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: This is the transport faculty or the boarding school.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You've pointed to the transport faculty, and you mentioned the boarding school. Could you tell us which army had that faculty under its control.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: The BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace, I take it that the description for the transcript is not sufficient to follow the testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I wonder whether the scale of the map is really suitable for this degree of detail. I recall there is another map which the Prosecution used of the Ilijas area. I wonder whether that might be more suitable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Say for Witness AD. Is that what you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. And perhaps if we could assist, perhaps the Prosecution could see if we have some copies and help the Defence in that regard if is convenient to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least, Ms. Pilipovic, it goes rather in detail. I don't know whether we either can zoom in or whether you use this map or not. But if so, then we need a clear description of what the witness pointed at. And I think also the map should be moved such that we can follow the way the witness is pointing to certain areas. So I leave it up to you whether you would prefer to continue with another map or that you would prefer to continue with this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I think that my colleague is referring to Map 3724, and I have part of that map. It Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. wouldn't be a problem to show the witness that map, too. But I would just like to make use of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then please ask the witness to point again at the places he indicated before so that we have a better look at it. And if necessary, that the map be moved and zoomed in such a way that we get a clear view of what he points at. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, could you just use the pointer to point to the area from which the BH army tank opened fire. Could you please move your hand so that you can point to this with the pointer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have to be very careful with this map because it's an expensive one.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, could you move the map to the right, please, so that we can see the image that is clear. Yes. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just point to the area --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: -- from which the BH army opened fire from attack and used anti-armour weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: As I said, it was from elevation Zuc, 850, up to the Orlic elevation, 876.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned fortified bunkers. Can you indicate the area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, for the transcript, the witness points a little bit to the left and above where it reads "1K" on what is I take it by now known to the parties as Zuc hill just north of the western extension of the city of Sarajevo. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, you mentioned trenches and bunkers, and you said that these were fortified positions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you use the pointer to point to the trenches and the fortified bunkers, the areas where there were trenches and fortified bunkers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the area was called, if you know the name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Those bunkers were to the left at the place called Kute, or perhaps 200 or 300 metres from the place called Kute. It was called Jezevi. There was a crossroads there. And to the right, towards the Vis elevation, which is above the number 2 here. And something has been marked with a blue felt tip here so you can't see it very well. From here up to Jezevi, as far as Jezevi, there were trenches, communicating trenches, and bunkers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How long was that line?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But for the sake of the transcript, I'd like to state that the witness pointed to the area marked in blue. And from number 1, where it says the 1st Motorised Brigade, and number 2, the 2nd Motorised Brigade, he said that this was the area of Jezevi.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And you said the Vis area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that this was an area in which the BH army had bunkers and trenches.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the transcript, the witness was pointing at the blue dotted line on the northwestern flank of what we just described as being Zuc hill. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, you have shown us this area, too, the area in which there were bunkers and trenches. You pointed to the transport faculty on the map and said that this was a firing position, and you also pointed to a tank. Were there any other places, fortified positions, in your opinion, that you could identify on this map and where you fired from positions that you had taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: In the depth of the Zuc elevation, 850, there were other positions because the army that was on the line. When there was action by the BH Army, you could hear explosions. You could hear shots being fired. I assume this was from mortars. I don't know of what calibre.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the sake of the transcript, the witness has pointed to the area where explosions could be heard, according to what the witness said, the sound of explosions which resulted from shots being fired from mortars, that's northwest, in a northwestern part of the map between number 2, I think it's number 2 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which is in the Zuc area. That's what I understood.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the transcript, is where a little flag appears with a number 2 in it close to the northwestern flank. And could you ask the witness again to point at the transport faculty because I might have missed that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see this black rectangle?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, could you tell us what road that is? Was the direction -- that is a little closer, point us a little closer which would enable us to locate the transport faculty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Well, about 200 and 250 metres from the Unis factory.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And where is the Unis factory located? Can you identify it on the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we first describe for the transcript where is the rectangle that the witness pointed at. That is on this map close to Vogosca village in the middle between the two red dots being part of the red dotted line, the two red dots being up highest north of this line close to Vogosca. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, could you explain the following for us, given your professional qualifications: Do you know what this sign means, Brag?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Brigade artillery group.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what a Brag, brigade artillery group, consisted of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether that was a location? Can you tell us whether that was the location of the brigade artillery group? Is that where the artillery was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Where I was situated?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell us whether throughout the period of the conflict up to August 1994, did the brigade artillery have its positions in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you personally know whether in the course of 1994 an agreement was signed on the withdrawal of the artillery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of such an agreement being signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During that period, after the agreement on the withdrawal of the artillery had been signed, did you receive similar orders on withdrawing the artillery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were any discussions with UNPROFOR members with regard to your artillery withdrawing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: As far as I could tell, they had allowed us to remain there because we were under their control. Their side controlled us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "controlled," can you tell us whether UNPROFOR was present there, too? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes, from the very first day.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you personally know how the routes for the withdrawal of the artillery were determined? Was there a proposal? Was there a suggestion as to how this should be done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't understand the question very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: We mentioned the agreement on the withdrawal of the artillery. Are you aware of the contents of that agreement as far as giving directions for withdrawal are concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Well, the artillery was to withdraw 20 kilometres from the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I in between ask for a clarification of one answer. Ms. Pilipovic has asked you whether the UNPROFOR was present there, and your answer was: "Yes, from the very first day." The very first day of what? Of the conflict? Of the existence of the agreement? On the first day since you were there? What did you mean to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the agreement was signed on withdrawal of the artillery, artillery that had a calibre that exceeded 12.7 millimetres, that when they were present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. Thank you for your clarification.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, we mentioned the UNPROFOR presence. Do you know whether before this agreement was signed, do you know whether UNPROFOR came to this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you are telling us that you personally never contacted members of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, in order to finish using this map before we have a break, I would like to ask you another question. Were there any other firing positions or fortified positions, as you call them, which you could identify on this map? Were there positions that you fired at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: The commanders of the lines, who changed on a daily basis, they were in the best position to see from which parts of Zuc our positions were under the greatest threat so that at their request and with the approval of the relevant command, the superior command, we would disable those targets, those positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think it would be a good time to have a break now. And after the break, I will ask the witness to use the other map to designate -- to mark the positions, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whenever we are using the big map, because we should use a copy because this original document is, when it's manipulated too much on the ELMO and folded again and again, it might be damaged. So I suggest to the parties that when we are using this map, that we use one of the colour copies, and if necessary, I think there are two or three copies.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I'll bring the Defence's copy, if my colleague agrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For the transcript, Mr. Ierace is nodding which I understand to be yes. We'll adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam usher, if you would escort the witness into the courtroom, I'll take the opportunity to ask one question about the map we just used. I remember someone saying that a CD-ROM copy might be made available as well. And I'm wondering whether it does exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, you're correct. We did have it placed on to a CD. There's a problem with the software, so we've had it returned to be corrected. Just on the issue of maps, this may not be the time, but perhaps at some later stage today, I could give you some further information in response to some concerns that have been expressed about the maps. I've made some inquiries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I gave it some thought as well. But let's first continue. Mr. DP50, Ms. Pilipovic will continue to examine you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, before I continue with the examination-in-chief, I'd like to show the witness a section of a map that we spoke about before the break. Perhaps the witness could mark for us on this map, and I have a sufficient number of copies if the Chamber and the colleagues from the Prosecution wish to have the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, do you recognise the area that you were showing on the other map we looked at before the break? Do you recognise the area on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, could you mark for us the positions of your field gun, and also later on the positions of the battery. First of all, I'd like to ask you, what was the length of the area that was covered by your battery which you said was established some time in the second half of 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: The distance from Pticja Glava elevation point up to the first line of the BH army, was from about three, three and a half kilometres, sometimes even it was a greater distance. I can't quite remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And what was the length of the line, of the surface that was covered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: One to one and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On this map, in this area that you were stationed at, could you please mark with a black pen this area. Could you draw a line, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Inside the circle, could you please put number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness circled the elevation 805, Pticja Glava, on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, in this area that you marked with a circle, is that where the battery was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP, on this map, would you be able to mark the location of the transport faculty as the firing position, the firing point for you, and the road that was also a firing point for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: This black dot in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you put number 2 there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness marked with a number 2 the location of the transport faculty. It is located northwest from the location Balino Brdo, 608, if that is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, on this map, if it is possible, can you mark the area that you told us was the area of trenches and bunkers of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Shall I draw with the pen?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can draw a line, a line that you said was the area of trenches and bunkers. This area that you've just marked, is that also the area of Jezevi and Vis area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You can just draw a line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: This line here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the ELMO please zoom in a bit more so that we have a better view on the line. Perhaps move the map a bit to the left. If it could be zoomed in even more, that would be... Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, could you please mark number 3 there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, number 3 is the line of bunkers and trenches of the BH Army which ran from the area where Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. there is a word Kata [sic], in the direction --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Kute, Kute.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I apologise. Kute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the marking is done to avoid the necessity of making clear descriptions. So I think if everyone marks with 3, there's no specific need to repeat what is actually there and where it is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, can you mark for us the location or the position where the tank was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please put number 4 there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On this map, would you be able to mark the positions of field guns or Howitzers, as you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Also in the area of number 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you were speaking about detonations, and in your opinion, the positions where mortars fired from, can you tell us what area was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please, below the line that you drew under the word Jezera, could you just put number 5.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So this is the area that you mark as being that where the mortars were active from. And where you drew a line under Zuc, could you put number 6.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: That is also the area that you marked from where mortars fired. Is that how I should understand it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, when you were telling us about the distance between the lines of the BH Army in relation to the positions of your battery, which line did you mean? Did you mean line number 3? When you were speaking about the distance of about 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes, from the firing position up to the BH Army line. I can't tell you precisely. Three, three and a half kilometres. It all varied according to the layout of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, on this map, would you be able to mark the first lines of defence of the VRS, of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: With a dotted line. I'm sorry. I'm sorry, so that we have a difference.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You can put number 7 there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So with a number 7, with a dotted line, you marked the lines of the Army of Republika Srpska. Mr. DP50, when you've told us that when you received the information, you used your field gun accordingly, was this from this line that you received the information about how you should use your weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us in which way were you informed, were you told?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Via telephone, and also by the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Who was the superior command as far as you were concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: The commander of the Mixed Artillery Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any personal information or knowledge where the command was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you received orders to fire, can you tell us in which way did you, as a gunner of the field gun, how did you fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: When I was a gunner, most of the time the direct firing was used. That is, the target is visible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your opinion, was there another way of firing? You said this was a direct firing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes. There was indirect firing. In the event when you wouldn't see a target, that is, when I was the commanding officer of that unit, that is, of the battery, in the cases when, according to this map, when targets were fired four, five, six.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you clarify this for us, when you say "targets four, five, six," what did you mean by that? When we are talking about indirect firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Well, when you said in which sector was the tank, you asked me that question. So this line that was drawn, behind it is number 4, this is where the tank was. And earlier, I said that there was also either a field gun or a Howitzer that fired on our line. And the numbers marked 5 and 6, these are the locations from where, according to the information received from the commander from the line, mortars were active.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, if I've understood you correctly, you told us that numbers marked on this map, 4, 5, and 6, were targets for you that you couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Five and six could not be seen, while target number 4 could be seen, was visible, when they were firing, when that target was active, that, I mean, target number 4. Because from the position, it was possible to see the slopes of Zuc hill that were steep. And so it was possible to see that from the firing position. You could see the tank firing or a field gun or a Howitzer firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, are you telling us that as far as post 4 is concerned or position 4, there were situations where you were able to see the target? And what kind of targeting or firing did you use then when you could see number 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: It was both direct and indirect.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP50, when you're telling us about the way of targeting or firing from a field gun, you said that it was done in an indirect and direct way. You as a person who was a gunner on the field gun did you know about the margin of error and the possibility of error?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us in which situations were errors possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: First of all, human factor. Weather conditions, which means that the air temperature, if it is too low, if it is too high, if there is wind, if there is rain, all weather conditions can influence the bullet trajectory. All of them were relevant for the possibilities of error.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, you said both human factor and weather conditions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I think you didn't tell us what was the reason or what -- can you explain about the human factor. You didn't elaborate on that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Speed, and the targets were not properly calibrated. How should I explain this? And the actual calculator sometimes - how should I explain this - could make an error in numbers. There could be calculating errors.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you mentioned speed, what did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Well, I wanted to say was that when there was order to fire on these targets, as soon as possible, as rapidly as possible, because that line that we were firing on was so much at risk that the BH Army could have entered Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction: The line that we were firing from was so much at risk that the BH army could have entered Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, when firing from a field gun, what is the maximum distance, for instance, in indirect firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: For field gun B1, maximum range or maximum distance was, as I said, 7.5 to 8 kilometres. But we fired possibly up to 5, 5.5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly that you did not fire over 5 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry. Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In indirect firing, what was the maximum range?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: 5 to 5.5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us this about possible distance, possible range, or could you perhaps just elaborate so that I don't lead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: We fired up to 5 kilometres. We didn't fire any further than that because there was no need to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, when you told us about the possibilities of direct and indirect targeting, you, as you, gunner, and later on as the commanding officer of the battery, can you tell us, what is the way of targeting that you used for the most part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: When I was on the Zis field gun, most of the time we used direct targeting because I saw the targets. But when I came into charge of the B1 battery field guns, there was a person calculating in the unit for the targets in respect of indirect firing, and even for targets for which direct firing could be used.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you told us that when you were by yourself, most of the time you were using direct targeting. So how did you do that? You saw those targets. Did you use anything, any utensil for that, did you see with the naked eye?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I was using binoculars.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you were using binoculars, did you receive the binoculars? Was it issued to you in the unit, or...?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No, I received it from a friend who was a hunter.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you spoke about the men who were in your battery, can you tell us whether these men were in some way trained to handle the field guns?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: 90 per cent of the manpower in the unit were trained. As far as the gunners were concerned, those who were working the field guns, that was 100 per cent of them were trained.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you're telling us about 90 per cent manpower trained, you're speaking about your battery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No, I'm speaking about the entire manpower.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Of your battery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. DP50, can you tell us, in the field, the area that is to be covered, that area that you covered, how wide was it? You marked it on the map, but can you tell us how big was it? Can you tell us the length of that area, the width of that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Well, the area we covered was about one to one and a half kilometres, plus width of Zis field gun. I could also reach the -- or had within my range the transport faculty.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you said that in your battery, 90 per cent of the manpower were trained, what was necessary for someone to be able to handle a field gun? What qualifications were necessary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: First of all, the men who joined the unit, they came with artillery military specialty. So they had the basic knowledge about what is to be done with a field gun. So the gunner was trained. He knew how to handle all the elements. The crew knew how to load the field gun. They knew where they should shelter, how to behave when being part of a crew of a field gun. And therefore, they also could be safe while working with the field gun.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, while you were at your positions, while you were responsible for this field gun, as you say, what sort of view did you have? Did you have a view in the direction of the town? When I say "in the direction of the town," I'm referring to the open part of the town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No. No. Because it wasn't possible to see Sarajevo from the Zuc hill, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, did you yourself ever receive orders --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, the last answer given by the witness reads: "Because it wasn't possible to see Sarajevo from the Zuc hill, not at all." That seems not well understandable, in view of the testimony of the witness. Could you please repeat your answer whether you could see the city of Sarajevo. You gave a reason why you couldn't see, as far as I understand. Could you repeat that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From my firing position, I personally couldn't see the town of Sarajevo. As far as I know, the town of Sarajevo is composed of ten municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why couldn't you see the...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because it was at a distance from where I was, and the Zuc hill was in front of me. So I had no need for the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's distance and view obstructed by Zuc hill.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as you say, there was the Zuc hill, which was an obstacle, and it wasn't necessary for me to fire at the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just asking about the view you had, not whether you fired. What could you see from the city of Sarajevo? Nothing at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, did you ever receive orders to fire at certain targets? You mentioned what the target were for you, apart from the targets that you've mentioned. Were you ordered to fire at certain other targets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Well, there were the targets that I have mentioned, the commander of the line who was at the line and who knew where fire, infantry fire, was being opened from or artillery fire. So as far as those targets are concerned, we didn't fire. We didn't fire randomly at those targets.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Ierace, is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If I could just have a moment to collect my documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. DP50, you'll now be examined by counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you told us that the -- your responsibility changed during the period that you were in the company. By August 1994, did you have a rank?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please answer the question, or is there any difficulty in answering the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can answer the question, but for the reasons of safety, I'm not answering it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll turn into private session, and then no one will hear anything. So it's not only your face that cannot be seen, but even your words cannot be heard by anyone out of this courtroom. We'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please answer the question. We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zoran Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know someone by the name of Srecko Gracanin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there a unit of artillery attached to the Vogosca Brigade apart from the battalion you've told us about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was Zdravko Djukic the deputy commander of the battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know what type of weaponry, that is, artillery weaponry, the brigade had apart from your battery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No, I don't, because I was at my firing position all the time. So I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, was there any change of personnel between your battery and other batteries, artillery batteries, within the brigade, the Vogosca Brigade? Did men sometimes move between them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: There were changes, but not between units, because there were young men. They wanted to be educated, so they enrolled in university, and this is why they would leave the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that you received your orders on telephone lines. Were they open lines, in other words, were you able to hear communications between others on the same network?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No. I only had a communication line with my superior, that involved my superior and myself. No one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that you heard mortars being fired from the other side of the front line which you thought was three to three and a half kilometres away. Did you hear artillery weapons being fired from your side of the line?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not sure that the witness said that he heard shots being fired. I think that when the witness spoke about mortars, I think that his answers were different. As far as I can remember, and I'll try to check this in the transcript, he used a different word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's check it in the transcript and see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Page 28, line 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is an assumption in the answer as well, Mr. Ierace. At least, there's a sufficient basis for the question. But perhaps you refer to the answer of the witness with great precision, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, do you recollect that you had told us that you could hear explosions from the enemy side of the front line in the region of Zuc? And that you assumed that what you could hear was the sound of mortars being fired. Do you recall saying that, words to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I said the commander of the line heard shots being fired, and he reported on this. And in normal conditions, you can hear mortar fire at a distance of 800 metres. So this didn't involve me; the commander of the line heard this, who was in contact with the BH Army, who had contact lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, may I ask you not to look to the party who is not examining you. Ms. Pilipovic, page 28, your summary of the testimony of the witness is that he heard mortars being fired. Let me just read it. According to what the witness said, the sound of explosion which resulted from shots being fired from mortars, that's the northwestern part of the map between -- you said explosions could be heard. So that's the way you summarised the testimony of the witness. It's my view, not my proper now to object against when Mr. Ierace understood the answer to be the same. Mr. DP50, when you answered that question, you said that you heard it, then it was summarised by Ms. Pilipovic, and then you confirmed that again. So you didn't speak about any commanders at that very moment. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, I'll read part of your answer word for word. "In the depth of the Zuc elevation, 850, there were other positions because the army that was on the line, when there was action by the BH army, you could hear explosions. You could hear shots being fired. I assume this was from mortars. I don't know of what calibre." I suggest to you that you were clearly saying that you heard explosions, you could hear shots being fired, you assumed on the basis of what you heard they were mortars. But on the basis of what you heard, you couldn't work out what calibre those mortars were. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Can I explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
