utterances.text: Sir, if you could just answer the question. I suggest to you that you told us earlier that indeed you did hear the explosions that you assumed to be mortars being fired. Do you agree or do you disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: An explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you agree or disagree?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace asked you whether you would agree that your earlier testimony was that you did hear explosions that you assumed to be from mortars being fired. First the question is whether you told this, and then if there's an explanation, that might be the next question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Testimony. Yes, you want to give an --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Firing a shell from a mortar is one thing. And the shell hitting the ground is another matter. Hearing the sound of a mortar shell being fired is more difficult, it's more difficult to hear it. When a shell hits the ground, the sound is a lot louder. That's what I was referring to. And the commander said that shells had been fired from that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The words of your answer in part were "you could hear shots being fired." You did not say you could hear shots landing. Do you remember saying these words: "You could hear shots being fired"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes, shells. But from tanks and from guns, field guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Your next words were: "I assume this was from mortars. I don't know of what calibre."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Well, there were mortars, but I don't know of what kind because I was informed of this by others.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, from your battery position, did you hear tanks firing from your side of the line at any stage in that period, from September 1992 until August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you hear Howitzers being fired from your side of the line in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: From a distance, but I don't know from which part, from which area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How far away do you think you heard them being fired from, from your side of the line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Well, between 5 and 6 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In which direction from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Behind me. But it wasn't as if they were firing over me. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I take it you're not able to tell us from what you heard which direction they were firing in except they weren't firing over you. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No, no. The shell that was fired didn't go over my firing position, it didn't go in the direction of the town. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. On how many occasions did you hear a Howitzer being fired from your side of the line in that period approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Two or three times a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And on how many occasions, if at all, in that same period did you hear multiple rocket launchers being fired from your side of the line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At all?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure that the witness mentioned multiple rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He doesn't have to. I mean, for cross-examination, there's no -- it's not a reference to what the witness testified earlier. It's a new question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I think that the witness should first of all be asked whether he knows what such a weapon is and whether he ever had the opportunity of seeing such a weapon, if we are talking about firing from multiple rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is not whether he saw them, but whether he heard them. That's a question that is admissible. But let me first try to find out. Are you aware of any multiple -- now I'm confused as well. Are you aware of any multiple rocket launchers being fired when you were at your positions, from your side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What about mortars? Did you hear any mortars being fired between September 1992 and August 1994, from your side of the line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: From my side, to the right of me, I heard from the locals that they were located somewhere, the mortars were located somewhere. But I don't know in which part.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, did you ever hear them fired in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Never heard any mortars, never heard any rocket launchers. Don't recall whether you heard any tanks. Howitzers a couple of times. Did you hear any other artillery pieces being fired, apart from your battery, from your side from September 1992 to August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: As far as I know, I told you about the Howitzer and the mortars, that I didn't hear them. As far as tanks are concerned, yes, because they have a huge destructive power for destroying bunkers. But from which location, that, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you hear any other artillery pieces being fired from your side of the line in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Well, only field guns. 30 and 40 millimetre calibre ones, as far as I know. I can't be certain. They were right behind the line of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, why is it that when I point it out to you in summary, your answers to these questions, you changed your evidence in relation to tanks, whereas earlier you said you didn't remember whether you heard tanks, you now say "as far as tanks are concerned, yes, because they have a huge destructive power for destroying bunkers. But from which location, that, I don't know." Why did you change your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: As far as I know, I said about the tank. As far as the Howitzers and the mortars are concerned...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Let me read to you your earlier answer and the question. Page 51, line 23. Question: "Now, from your battery position, did you hear tanks firing from your side of the line at any stage in that period, from September 1992 until August 1994?" Answer: "I don't remember.". Do I take it that now you do remember hearing them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Eight years have passed since the war, and many traumas I went through. So anything could have happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, the problem is not that you might have forgotten about what happened eight years ago. The issue Mr. Ierace is raising is that in your previous answer, which is just two or three minutes ago, you said that you didn't remember any tanks being -- hearing any tanks being fired, and that two or three minutes later you give a different answer. That's the issue, not whether you have forgotten something over eight years. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace. Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, listening to the explanation and the answer, I think that the question that Mr. Ierace asked in respect of whether the witness had heard the firing from a tank was in relation to his line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which is line 21 of 53, of page 53. So we're speaking about a line here. I think the question at that time was accurate in respect of the line. Perhaps there should be some clarification added rather than lead the witness in suggesting -- that's how I understand the lines the witness had marked, where his line was, where his position was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the accused could keep his voice down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there's any need to confer with General Galic, would you please take your headphones off and do it as silent as possible. I'll go through all the tanks of the last ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the interests of saving time, might the witness be taken from the courtroom because there's something I wish to say in relation to the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom. Before doing so, I'll try to analyse what we heard until now. That is, on page 51, line 18, on a question when I think Mr. Ierace sought confirmation of an earlier answer, where the witness said: "You could hear shots being fired" and then the witness said: "Yes, shells, but from tanks and from guns, field guns." And then a few lines further, the question was: "Now, from your battery position, did you hear tanks firing from your side of the line at any stage in that period, from September 1992?" And then he said: "I don't remember." So first, his answer was that you could hear shots being fired, and specifically asked whether it was from positions on his side of the line, he said: "I don't remember." Then we have tanks again in page 54, line 2. That's general, not related to any of the lines. Never heard any mortars, never heard any rocket launchers. Don't recall whether you heard any tanks. And then the next answer was, "as far as I know, I told you about the Howitzer and the mortar, that I didn't hear them. As far as tanks are concerned, yes, and these were tanks from the side of the lines that were under the control of the witness. At least that's what the question was about. So when he earlier said he didn't know if he heard tanks fired but didn't know whether any tanks were fired on his side of the line, on page 54, he confirms that he did hear tanks being fired from his side of the line because that was what the question was about. So Mr. Ierace, so I tried first to analyse what happened during the testimony. Let me just see whether there's any further -- yes, then you said that the witness changed his position. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just two points quickly, Mr. President. After I first asked the question, I then asked him about Howitzers, and he had no difficult in saying that he heard Howitzers firing from some distance away, not close to where he was. So that confirms his understanding of the question. And secondly, I think it's inappropriate for my learned colleague to state the objection in the terms that she did in the presence of the witness. If the witness is now asked questions in re-examination about this issue, and if the answers are in accordance with what Madam Pilipovic has said she wondered, perhaps he thought, then the evidence is deprived of probative value, the witness having heard the words of Madam Pilipovic's objection. So I simply ask that any further objections not be made in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or in such general terms that it's only understandable for lawyers, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I thought the witness had a headset, and therefore couldn't hear what I was saying, so didn't hear what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, if he has a headset, everything you say will come to him in the original language. So if he has his headset on, then I take it that he fully understands whatever has been said. Perhaps this is good to know also for witnesses still to come. Apart from that, I noticed that the witness seems to look at the screen even -- I don't know whether there appears any text, but I cannot exclude that because I can't see it from here. Madam usher, could the witness please be escorted into the courtroom again. And may I urge the Defence to be very careful with the objections. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you were asked questions about the heavy weapons exclusion agreement. Did that become effective from midday on the 19th of February, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date. I just know when the agreement came into force, we stayed and whether it was UNPROFOR, IFOR, or SFOR, they wouldn't let us go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you stay at the position of your battery from that date until August 1994, or did you move somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: We were there all the time. SFOR wouldn't let us go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Together with the rest of your battery crew, you all stayed there until August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes, myself and all the weapons. They all stayed there. And the men as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Given that the weapons could not be fired, did you or your men take some time off and leave that area, and perhaps mix with other members of your brigade, if not your battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: We had to look after the weapons. We were working in shifts, you understand, two days on, two days off.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Two days on, two days off, and nothing to fire for six months. Is that the position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: We couldn't fire. SFOR wouldn't let us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before the agreement came into effect, how would you take delivery of the shells that you would fire from your battery? Were they brought to you, perhaps on a truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And when the truck left, would it still have some shells on it for delivery elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: A small quantity arrived, and it was just for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever ask the deliverers whether there were any other batteries in the area such as yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I didn't. Most of the time we were just mucking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know whether your battalion had rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you understand that it's a little odd to hear you say that, given that you were in this position for such a period of time, you were the commander of your battery, in a static position, and that you tell us that you don't know whether your battalion had rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps there was, and perhaps there wasn't. If I had seen it personally, then I would have said that it was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You understand I'm not asking you whether you saw it personally, but whether you had any knowledge. You understand that, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [No audible answer]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Do you know whether your battalion had any mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does that mean you don't know or it didn't have any?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know whether it had any Howitzers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know whether your brigade had any tanks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that through your binoculars, you could see Zuc. I take it there were times when you were firing in Zuc in company with batteries from elsewhere firing on Zuc. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When that happened, were you able to work out where the fire was coming from, that is, the fire other than from your battery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Since the settlement or the town of Vogosca is in a valley, both the firing and the detonations would be as they happened in a valley, and they would echo, because it was a valley. It was impossible to know where the firing was coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps you didn't understand my question. In relation to firing at ABiH positions on Zuc where you had a direct line of sight and the assistance of your binoculars, when there was coordinated fire, were you able to work out where the fire was coming from, that is, the explosions as a result of fire from other than your battery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: It wasn't possible to hear from the detonations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You're saying that you couldn't hear the shells explode on Zuc. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Zuc was only about 4 kilometres away, wasn't it, from your position, the top of Zuc?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There was a direct line of sight, you've told us. You could see it through the binoculars. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: But the slopes of Zuc facing me, facing my firing position, which means the line that I drew.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, when you fired in the direct mode, in other words, you were firing at a target that you could see, and that target was on Zuc, did you hear the explosions that you could see through your binoculars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Some, yes; and some, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you tell us that some of the shells that you fired with your artillery you could see explode on Zuc, but you couldn't hear them. Is that correct? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: A shell that I would fire, and I would see the target, I could see it. And when the target, like a tank or mortars were targeted, then I couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever hit the tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: At those distances, I wasn't able to. But at least I disabled it from being active. What I mean is -- how should I explain that? It was a kind of firing like disabling firing, firing to disable. It wouldn't be a direct firing or a direct targeting. Perhaps something was around it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, how many times did you do that, did you disable the tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: According to my information, things that I know personally, there were two tanks on Zuc. One was disabled. Now, whether I had done it or the troops that were on the line, I don't know. Because they had hand-held rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Between September 1992 and August 1994, do you say that there was a tank disabled throughout that period on Zuc?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: From September 1992, is this how I should understand your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I was on sick leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. When did you first learn that there was a disabled tank on Zuc?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: In the second half of 1993. And I was on sick leave from September to January, that is, from September 1992 until beginning of January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As you understand it, was there ever a period of time up until August 1994 from 1993 when there were two tanks undisabled firing from Zuc?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sorry. Was there any period in 1993 or up until August 1994 when, as you understood it, there were two active tanks on Zuc?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Then why is it that the first we heard from you of there being two tanks was just a few minutes ago? Why didn't you mention the second tank before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: You didn't ask me. I said a tank. And a tank is a mobile. Understand? Tank, that means can be in all the places. Perhaps there were several tanks. I know about one that I saw was destroyed. But again, after a certain period of time, news came from the line that from the sector 850, Orlic elevation point, a tank was active because they could hear the engine running.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, correct me if I am wrong, perhaps I'm mistaken. Didn't you tell us a number of times in answer to questions asked by the learned lawyer for the Defence that there was "a tank" operating in position number 4, as you marked on the map? You always referred to "a tank," not "tank"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And the first time you mentioned two tanks is when I asked you if you ever hit the tank. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I said perhaps there were two tanks, and perhaps that one tank was in one place, and perhaps that's the place that was destroyed. Perhaps a second tank came. I can't claim that this tank that was destroyed, that that was the tank that was at the elevation point between --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I want to make sure I understand your answer. It reads: "I said perhaps there were two tanks and perhaps that one tank was in one place and perhaps that's the place that was destroyed. Perhaps a second tank came." Do I now understand your evidence to be that you're not sure there was ever a second tank? Is that what you're saying? You're not sure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember I asked a few minutes ago if at any stage there were two tanks active on Zuc in 1993 up to August of 1994, and you said yes? Do you remember giving that evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that perhaps my learned colleague could give us the reference, where was it that the witness had said that, so that the witness doesn't get confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The rule is that if it was only a very short time ago, it was not necessary. But we'll find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: It's page 63, line 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll read the question to you, and your answer a few minutes ago. Question: "Was there any period in 1993 or up until August 1994 when, as you understood it, there were two active tanks on Zuc?" Answer: "Yes." Do you remember being asked that question and giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the witness be shown two photographs. They are exhibits P3764 and P3765. I might indicate these have been produced during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The one photograph you would like to start with...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If both of them can be shown to the witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think on the ELMO now, sir, we have a photograph of an artillery gun connected to a truck. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And the Zis 3 that we see being towed by the truck.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that the -- well, I'll rephrase it. Is that the artillery piece that you had, that you had, on Pticja Brdo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, look at the other photograph. Is that the M48, and I think at various times you've also referred to it as the B1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, you were asked what was the range of the B1. And you told us that you only fired it up to five or five and a half kilometres because that's all you needed to fire it. But it had a range I think you said up to 8 kilometres. Is that correct, the B1, or as it's referred to here, the M48?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: B1, you mean B1, you mean this field gun up to 8 kilometres, but we used it for distances for up to 5 kilometres because we had no need to fire over 5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. You didn't tell us about the other one, that is, the Zis. Did it have a maximum range of 13 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I said about 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And over what range did you use it? What was the maximum range that you ever used it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: In the area of Zuc, so those lines that we drew, that was the range. 3.5, 4 kilometres. I'm not quite sure. And the transport faculty. I don't know what the range is. And it was about 5.5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, although you only used it to fire as far as Zuc, 3.5 to 4 kilometres, it was capable of firing into the city, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Because there was no need to do that because I had no orders whatsoever to fire at the city --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP50, may I interrupt you. Would you please carefully listen to the questions. The question was not whether there was any need to fire with this weapon into the city, but whether the weapon was capable, that means whether you could if you would have wanted to do so, to fire into the city. Now would you please carefully listen to the question so that your answer is to the question. Yes, so the question was whether with this weapon of which you said the maximum range was 12 to 13 kilometres, whether you could fire into the city from your position. The question is not whether you did or whether you wanted, but whether you could.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I think -- yes. One moment, please. Mr. Ierace, if you could find a suitable moment soon to have a break, let's say within the next couple of minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right, now, the B1, is that sometimes known as the Tito gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Is it sometimes referred to as a mountain gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And is the reason for that the fact that it can be disassembled, in other words, it can be pulled apart rather easily and transported over rough terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible to disassemble it. But because it's an old field gun, so all the parts like nitrates and oil, leakage can happen. So in the war it was never disassembled. But in peacetime, it is possible to disassemble.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that. Thank you, Mr. President, that's a suitable time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom before we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one question before we go to have a break: The Defence knows that one witness who is supposed to come next has been waiting since 12.00. But he travelled all day yesterday, and arrived this morning. So perhaps could we have the information whether he's going to start testimony today, bearing in mind that he's had a very tiring journey. Perhaps it would be possible to inform the victims and witness unit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Your question. Mr. Ierace, how much time would you still need for the cross-examination of the witness? You've taken until now one hour as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you assist me with the Prosecution time, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One hour until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And -- I'm sorry, the Defence time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Defence time was one hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I imagine that I'll take about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that would mean that if we would restart at 1.00, that we might even start with the next witness, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Without giving any guarantee, I could not exclude either that we would start with the next witness even today. So the Chamber would appreciate if the witness would remain available, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could I say, Mr. President, according to our figures, there was a 9 or 10-minute break in the middle of my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't -- I don't know whether it was 9 or 10 minutes. But there was some time when the witness left the courtroom. Yes, I do understand that you've taken, if the time would be would be deducted, when the witness left the courtroom, and what we discussed should not be reducted from the Prosecution time, you would have another 45 minutes. You would use that time, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'll try very hard not to, Mr. President. I expect I'll be finished in half an hour. I'll try to finish in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that is the case, I can't guarantee that we would not start with the next witness. It all depends also on how much time you would need for re-examination and how many questions the Judges would have.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could assist, there was that issue of maps which would take 5 minutes or so, if you were interested in using the time productively without going on to the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, let's just assume that we'll be a few questions in re-examination, that there might be a few questions from the Bench, and that we would need some time for maps, then the witness and victims unit could be informed that we'll not start with the next witness today. Yes. We'll adjourn until 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I was informed that you might even finish more quickly with the present witness. But, Madam Registrar, is just checking, but the next witness might have left already, and I'm not going to ask him to come back for a couple of minutes if he has left the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry about that, Mr. President. I reviewed my remaining questions over the break, and I think I can finish fairly quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll see whether, but we're not going to ask the witness to come back if he left the building. Then, could you please escort Witness DP50 back in the courtroom, Madam usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, so as to assist the Trial Chamber, some of the next questions relate to the evidence by the investigator by the name of Kucanin, as you may recollect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: May I ask the witness be shown the second map shown to the witness by Defence counsel. I don't recollect the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the map be placed on the ELMO so that circled area number 1 is in the centre of the screen. Perhaps the -- thank you. And if we could zoom in. Thank you. Would you please place the pointer on the circle around Pticja Glava.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. There's a town which appears immediately to the bottom right of the circle. Would you place your pointer on that. I think it's Krivoglavci. Place your pointer again on the circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please pronounce that name for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Krivoglavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Krivoglavci. Thank you. There were mortars in that position, I suggest to you, between September 1992 and August 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think we should bear in mind that the fact that from 1992 until January 1993, the witness was on sick leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm happy to rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that in 1993 and in 1994, up until August of that year, there were mortars in that area. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm suggesting to you that the Sarajevo Romanija Corps had a battery of mortars in that area in 1993 and 1994. Do you agree or do you disagree, or do you say that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see on the map to the right, and above Vogosca, a town called Blagovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that in 1993 and 1994, the Sarajevo Romanija Corps had tanks and mortars in that area. Do you agree or disagree or do you say that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You see on the map a place called Paljevo. To the left --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that in 1993 and 1994, there were either mortars or artillery or both in that area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What specifically was in that area by way of artillery or mortars?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I think there were Howitzers there. I couldn't hear mortars being fired. I'm not saying anything about mortars, but since the explosion that you hear when a Howitzer is fired is very loud, one could hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there parts of Vogosca which were occupied by Muslim residents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, in 1993 and 1994, to your knowledge, were there parts of Vogosca in which resided persons who identified with the cause of the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you understand that Vogosca had civilians living in it in 1993 and 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Are you referring to the town of Vogosca? I mean to say, the neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The town.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Whether there were Muslims in the town. Is that your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, as you phrase it, Muslims. Were there Muslims living in Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that civilian areas of Vogosca were shelled in 1993 and 1994. Do you agree or disagree or say that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am suggesting to you that in that period of time, areas which were occupied by, as you call it, Muslims, were deliberately shelled by forces of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I have told you, as far as I can remember, I wouldn't like it to seem as if I said something mistakenly again. In the town of Vogosca, there were Muslims. They lived in an area where there were Serbs and Croats and Muslims. That's what I said. And the part, if that is what you're after, where the Bosniaks lived, I don't know whether there were any inhabitants there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that shelling from Paljevo hit the Rajlovac area and Buca Potok, and indeed the entire lower part of Sarajevo. Do you agree, disagree, or do you say that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the map you have drawn for us the sections of the confrontation lines that were of particular relevance to your battery. When --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When the forces of your side, on either side of that section of the front line that you have marked, wanted the assistance -- the assistance of artillery, who provided it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: My battery and I, and I said that there were 30 and 40 millimetre guns there that were located behind the line. I think this is what I said a few minutes ago, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And is it your understanding that those guns provided support to the troops from your army on both sides of the section of the front line that you have marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: First of all, whereabouts were the positions of the 30 and 40 millimetre guns? Perhaps you could point to them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness points to an area --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Four to five hundred metres behind the line. Perhaps even further away.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The Witness pointed to an area to the left, immediately to the left, of the number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please place your pointer back on the line. And place your pointer at the end of the bottom left-hand part of the line and keep your pointer there, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you show us the direction of the confrontation lines of your army from that point. Show us where the line went from that point, with the pointer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Indicates.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know the position of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps front lines further south and west from that point that you have marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I know the line in the direction of Vogosca. But from this point here and in this direction, no, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Although you do not know it with precision, if that part of the front line needed artillery support, where would that artillery support come from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness has answered. He already answered that question put to him by my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic. You could look at that in different ways. The question has been answered. The witness says he doesn't know. So there's no need at this point to go into further detail in respect of this objection. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Although you tell us you do not know, do you have any idea at all where artillery support came from for that part of the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: In the depth behind my firing positions. In this area here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. I'm not sure which line we're discussing now, whether the one that the witness has drawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I missed what the witness was pointing at. Was that line numbered 7 or...? I see it's somewhere else. It seems to have created some confusion. Would you please take care that it becomes clear, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The area indicated by the witness during the last answer was in the vicinity of the towns which appear on the map as Atovici, in that general area. And I think slightly to the northeast from that town.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you telling us from that area came artillery support for the part of the SRK front line to the southwest of the portion that you have marked and numbered 7, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. But the witness said that he didn't know, so I don't see what the purpose of asking this question is. It would just be a matter of speculation. I think that the witness doesn't know how the line continues because on two occasions he said he didn't know. So I think that if we carry on examining the witness in this sense, the witness will only be confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But he is giving a few more answers about it. Mr. Ierace, you may proceed with your line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, could you ask the witness to point to the place again, because I cannot see number 7 anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, number 7 is the part of the front line that's already marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness, would you please point to the number 7 that you placed on the map earlier this morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now would you please point again to the area from which you think fire, that is, supporting artillery fire, came from, from the part of the front line which is southwest of portion number 7.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I can't say this with precision. I'm only indicating the area. I'm not showing the exact place. But this is the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I understand that. Now in relation to the portion of the front line to the northeast of the section that you have marked number 7, do you know where they drew artillery support from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown the first map. I think it's called C2. I think it was referred to as C2. Mr. President, I understand the next witness isn't available. If that's the case, I'll continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness is not available, as I understand. If we could finish with this witness today, that would be fine. And there might be questions, so please take that into consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. I will

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're going to use the copy at this very moment. It's not supposed to be marked. Mr. Ierace, could you please assist the usher to tell her what will be the relevant part.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, had you seen this map before you arrived in the courtroom this morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Had you seen a map like this one before it was shown to you this morning, either yesterday or the day before, or years ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: It was only possible a few years ago. Quite a few years ago in the sense that Sfora showed such maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What do you mean by Sfora?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: They had maps, S-F-O-R. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever see a map like this in 1993 or 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: In 1994 or 1995, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, on this map, we see that Pticja Glava had an altitude of 805 metres. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And correct me if I am wrong, Zuc has an altitude of around 850 metres. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When one looks at the terrain between Pticja Glava and Zuc, am I correct in saying that there is nothing in between of a similar altitude to Pticja Glava? In other words, you were on a high point, Zuc was on a high point, and there was nothing particularly high in between.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes, Pticja Glava wasn't as high as Zuc, and there's an empty space between Pticja Glava and Zuc. But Zuc descends -- how should I put it. It descends from an altitude of 850 metres. I'm referring to the altitude above sea level.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. Now, to the right of Pticja Glava, we see some symbols in red. Perhaps you could point to them. Each is within a circle, with circles adjoined by parallel lines.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. What do those symbols mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: This is the symbol for artillery weapons. This was my battery's symbol, and I don't know what this symbol is down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, the symbol you identified as depicting your battery is the one in the top circle, the one indicating artillery that you could not explain further is in the bottom circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I understand the bottom one to be identified by you as relating to artillery. Do you say that you don't know what it means beyond that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I was only interested in my weapons, what I should know as best I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean that -- correct me if I'm wrong, that during the war, you did see maps with that top symbol on them depicting your battery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many different maps did you see with symbols for your battery, or a symbol for your battery? Are we talking about just the one map or different maps from time to time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Well, three or four maps, perhaps even five.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were any of those maps shown to you by your superiors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: You mean my superior?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: He showed it to me, but without these symbols.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I asked you about maps with the symbol on it for your battery. How many such maps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Two or three. Not many.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were any of those two or three shown to you by your superior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that at the battery or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: At the battery.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever go to your superior's office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I didn't need to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We see a flag-type symbol over Vogosca. That is a triangle --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that when you fired, you used reference points. What were the reference points?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Reference points that denote a location of something, that is, of a target, XYZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Do you mean that you had prerecorded coordinates for targets that you were likely to need to hit in the future?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember that you told us this morning that you had reference points, and the commander of the line would guide you where fire was coming from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I said that they were orientation points. That's a different thing from a reference point. An orientation point is a facility which is visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Were they points that were designed to enable you to position the artillery guns quickly to hit particular targets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you fired, for instance, at the building in Vogosca that you told us about, did you have reference points that enabled you to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: That building is a large facility, and it is visible. That building itself was an orientation point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Even though you could see it, did you have coordinates for it? Did you have settings that you could adjust on the gun so that you could more accurately hit it with a shell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Only in certain cases. But that was very rare. If there was firing at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But you were able to hit the road, you told us. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Which road?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The road outside the building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Describe for us the target that you would hit in Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: You mean the transport faculty.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you ever --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: In front, the faculty, is 100 metres long, and about 50 metres wide. In front of the faculty, by the road --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right, did you not say earlier this morning that you targeted the road as well as the transport faculty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, would you please give us the source of that. Are you referring to page 34, line 24, 25? Because then in page 35, line 2, the answer might not be as clear as...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, yes, I'm referring to page 24, at line -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was referring to 34.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm referring to page 24, around line 18. Line 23, question: "Could you first of all point out the road. Could you point to the road and the transport faculty. You said that these positions were firing positions for you." And I think there's an earlier reference as well. I'm conscious of the time, Mr. President. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He mentioned the name of the road. He talked about the Vogosca/Pale Road. It's not that clear to me. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you target the road near the transport faculty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: As far as I know, this morning, I mentioned a road, Vogosca/Sumbulovac which was at risk because of the transport faculty.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I understand that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Ms. Pilipovic, is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, one question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. DP50, the sound of a field gun when a shell is fired, for instance, from the B1 field gun, I think that's what we said, the second photograph, not the Zis field gun. So the force, how loud is the firing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know about artillery, I think that it is most probably the loudest firing because the barrel is short.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you said the loudest firing, how can you make that comparison, the basis of what can you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Well, even if we compare it to a tank.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And when you are speaking about a position, Pticja Glava, 805 elevation point, can you tell us and describe for us in relation to 805 elevation, where were your tanks positioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Tanks or field guns?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I mean field guns.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Below the Pticja Glava elevation point.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps we could have a direction rather than elevation. Does below mean further south or further north?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would that further to the north of 805 or to the south or to the west or to the east? Or tell us in the direction of what village --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say it's below the top, it could be in all directions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, yes, yes, yes. I don't have the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it in the direction of Krivoglavci or is it in the direction north to Svrake --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not towards Svrake. May I have the map, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, the small one. From the top of the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, where number 1 is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is on the southeast --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's where it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I can see it well. Could we zoom in exactly on the -- yes, perhaps -- yes. One is written south of southeast from where it reads 806. Yes. It's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 805.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 805, yes. Thank you very much. Madam usher, the map can be removed. Judge Nieto-Navia has one question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We leave the map, Madam usher, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Could you point again to the area from which you were guessing that the southwestern line could get artillery support.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: This area here. Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes. Now, with the colour map, Madam Registrar...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Can I point now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Please do it again on that map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: It's not the area where you can find the symbol for the artillery group, to the south. Is it? Do you see the symbol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: No. The layout of the terrain is such, you understand, there's hill, valley, hill, valley. Goes up and down. So I showed you the possible location, but it may have been somewhere else. Because the valley has an influence on the noise of the detonation. If you hear it in the valley, it could mean -- it could have the sound as if it was fired from the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Do you see the symbol of the artillery group in that area? Do you see the symbol, the southern part, the symbol like the one you showed --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: To the south. South, south.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: This here. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Could be that the area you were pointing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I can't say for sure about this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've got a few questions for you, if the interpreters would permit us to take a couple of minutes. You told us about Paljevo, and you thought there were Howitzers there. You could hear it when they fired because the explosion is very loud. That's what you told us. You remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. When you heard these Howitzers being fired, from what position? Because I do understand that you have been in two different positions. Was this when you were at Pticja Glava or was this before when you were at Zuc? When did you hear the Howitzers? From what position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Well, from Pticja Glava, because that was behind me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From there, you heard the Howitzers. Do you know where these Howitzers -- they were not part of your battery. To what unit did they belong? Were they Howitzers in the battalion, or were they --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. Because that's a wooded area. I don't know that terrain. And of course, we were afraid to go there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What would be approximately -- you said it was just behind you. What would be approximately the distance between Pticja Glava and Paljevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: One and a half kilometres to two kilometres, depending on the layout of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you explain to us during your testimony when you were asked whether you ever heard Howitzers fired from your side of the line, you told us that it was from a far distance that you could hear it, and you mentioned 5 to 6 kilometres. Now you're telling us that Howitzers, at least what you thought to be Howitzers, were fired from Paljevo which was at a distance of approximately one and a half kilometre. What could explain these two, as far as I understand them, rather different answers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: You're right. The positions change. Because if a position is uncovered by the Muslim artillery, then that position has to change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because that still does not explain the difference in your answers because when asked about whether you heard Howitzers being fired, it was about the whole period of time. And you said only from a distance 5 to 6 kilometres. You didn't say 5 to 6 kilometres, but later on one and a half kilometre. The question was about the whole period. You didn't say one and a half kilometres; you said 5 to 6 kilometres. What explains, apart from the explanation you just gave, the difference in your two answers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP50
utterances.text: Only perhaps that I didn't know the distance exactly, and that's why I answered like that. That's what it may have seemed to me to start with. Because on the map, it looks differently. And when you walk on foot, then it is longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have no further questions. I think we can deal with the documents tomorrow. This concludes your testimony in this Court, Mr. DP50. And I'd like to thank you very much for having come the far way from where you live to The Hague and I'd like to thank you for answering all the questions of both parties and of the Bench. You're excused now. Madam usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I think talking about the maps would ask the impossible from the interpreters. So therefore, I'd rather do that tomorrow morning right at the beginning. I hope that it will take limited time. If there would be any communication between the parties so that they could offer us a solution together, that would be highly welcomed by the Chamber. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: at 1.50 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 27th day of November, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
